headline: 10 killed in Cox's Bazar resort fire; family of four still missing
summary: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Cox's Bazar claimed 10 lives, with a family of four, including two young daughters, still unaccounted for. Authorities are conducting DNA tests to identify the charred remains.
details: A devastating fire at TUPTUP Resto and Resort in Cox's Bazar's Ukhiya on Saturday morning killed 10 people. The blaze, which took two hours to control, left bodies charred beyond recognition, necessitating DNA tests for identification.

Relatives are desperately searching for a family of four: Nahidur Rahman Tuhin, his wife Afsana, and their daughters, 7-year-old Robaina and 3-year-old Sunaina. They had booked a room at the resort from October 16 to 18.

Nahidur, an official at Dhaka-based Grand Power Limited, worked in Shyamoli and lived in the capital. His family and colleagues have been unable to reach him or his family since the fire, causing immense anxiety.

Fire Service officials reported recovering six badly mangled bodies first, with four more, including a child and two women, found later in a toilet. Identification is impossible without DNA tests, and samples are being collected.

While several people were rescued alive, Nahidur and his family are not on the list of survivors. Police have information on the identities of six missing individuals, but four others are yet to be identified.

headline_marked: [[Youth arrested in Netrokona over journalist Alif Fakir's murder]]
headline: Youth arrested in Netrokona over journalist Alif Fakir's murder
summary: Police arrested a 22-year-old in Durgapur, Netrokona, who is the nephew of the prime suspect and was allegedly present during the shooting, carrying the weapons. He was also accused in a previous attack on the journalist.
details: Police have arrested a 22-year-old youth, Opurba, in connection with the shooting death of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir alias Alif Fakir in Durgapur, Netrokona. Opurba was apprehended from Durgapur municipal town shortly after midnight on Saturday.
Police claim Opurba was present at the scene during the killing and was carrying the bag containing the weapons. During primary interrogation, he reportedly admitted to the crime.

Opurba is identified as the nephew of the prime suspect shooter in the journalist's murder. The prime suspect is known as a 'contract for hire,' and the firearms used were allegedly kept in Opurba's custody.

The arrested youth was also an accused in a previous case filed last year. In November, journalist Alif Fakir was critically injured by sharp weapons in an attack at Teribazar Ghat area of Durgapur upazila.
Journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir Alif was shot dead by criminals on Thursday (October 15) around 8:15 PM. He was returning home after having tea at a stall in the Telanjia area of Durgapur upazila.
The victim's wife has filed a murder case with Durgapur Police Station. The case accuses seven to eight unidentified individuals in connection with the killing.
